transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We have one overnight rapid whole-genome sequencing run available, and three cases under consideration: Alder, Birch, and Cedar. I need to confirm four requirements for whichever case we select: clinical-actionability, specimen-adequacy, consent-scope, and payer-authorization. Once one case is confirmed to satisfy all four, I can finalize it without completing review of the others. Let's work through this efficiently. I'll invite each of you — genetics, laboratory operations, genetic counseling, and utilization management — to give me one concise direct confirmation for the case you've reviewed. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: For Case Alder, I completed the consent review this afternoon. The patient signed consent for both primary findings and secondary findings, so the approved report-scope field value must be recorded exactly as: primary_and_secondary_findings.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Case Alder has a medication-selection decision that depends on a rapid whole-genome result, so the clinical team has designated Alder as the clinically actionable priority for this overnight run. I documented this decision in my service note, but the note has not yet reached the laboratory queue.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: For Case Alder, the payer approved rapid whole-genome sequencing under authorization code UM-4821, with the authorization status recorded as approved. I received the approval notice but have not yet entered it in the laboratory authorization screen.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: For Case Alder, I verified at accession that the received specimen contains exactly 3.2 mL of viable blood, which meets our 3.0 mL minimum, and it must be processed with the standard EDTA extraction protocol.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, everyone. To summarize for Dr. Morris: Case Alder has all four requirements addressed. Consent scope is confirmed as primary_and_secondary_findings. Clinical actionability is confirmed but Dr. Shah's service note is pending transmission to the laboratory queue. Payer authorization is approved under code UM-4821, but Ms. Brooks has not yet entered it in the laboratory authorization screen. Specimen adequacy is confirmed at 3.2 mL viable blood with standard EDTA extraction protocol. Two administrative entries are still pending, so per policy the release plan should include commitments naming Dr. Shah for submitting the service note to the laboratory queue and Ms. Brooks for entering the authorization in the laboratory authorization screen before the run is released.
transcript.speaker: A4
